row.evidence: Endpoint Central's SAML guide says "To successfully log in using SAML, the user must be present both in the IdP and Endpoint Central", and its pricing page, edition matrix, help pages and Cloud API reference document no SCIM endpoint or IdP provisioning app.
row.notes: New row; Desktop Central is now sold as ManageEngine Endpoint Central (slug kept). Priced per endpoint bundle with 1 technician included, not per user, so per-user fields are null: Free (up to 25 endpoints), Professional $795/yr, Enterprise $945/yr, UEM $1,095/yr, Security $1,695/yr for 50 endpoints on-premises annual (Cloud annual $1,045 / $1,245 / $1,395 / $2,045). No SCIM: on-premises supports SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, OneLogin, AD FS, Auth0, Azure via custom/non-gallery apps) but the user must already exist in Endpoint Central (no JIT); technicians can also sign in with Active Directory authentication. Endpoint Central Cloud has a REST API (Zoho OAuth, DesktopCentralCloud.Admin.* scopes) to list, create, update and delete users (technicians) and manage roles; no IdP uses it for provisioning. Which edition first includes SAML is not stated. Status none by absence.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint documented in the pricing page, edition matrices, help sitemap, SAML guides or Cloud API reference. SAML requires the user to already exist in Endpoint Central.

endpoints.purpose: Update user (role, email, phone, computer scope)

user_api.notes: Endpoint Central Cloud API. The on-premises API (api-doc.html) covers inventory, patch and SoM; no user endpoints were found there.

okta.notes: No Endpoint Central app in the OIN (search for "endpoint central" returns no results). ManageEngine's guide builds a custom SAML 2.0 app with Create App Integration.

entra.notes: ManageEngine's Azure guide uses a non-gallery application; no Microsoft Learn tutorial found.

onelogin.notes: Vendor SAML guide lists OneLogin among supported IdPs; no provisioning.

Price of additional technicians is not shown on the static pricing page.
Whether the Cloud user API is available on every edition is not stated.
How Endpoint Central Cloud SSO (Zoho accounts) handles user creation is not documented on the pages checked.
